players.product: CPO solutions: prism micro-lens arrays (PMLA) and 1D & 2D fiber arrays

quarterly_data.signal: Investor relations head Joseph Huang (Chinese-language call; the machine transcript does not label speakers after the opening): Q3 2026 consolidated revenue was about NT$156.51 hundred million with a 42.2% gross margin and net income of NT$51.82 hundred million (EPS NT$39.62); the gross margin fell from Q2 mainly on poor yield of the new model and higher green-power costs; non-operating income was about NT$13.57 hundred million, including an FX gain of about NT$1.97 hundred million, and cash and equivalents were about NT$1109 hundred million. Management: Q3 capex was NT$81.8 hundred million, which includes most of the recent land purchases, and depreciation NT$20.4 hundred million.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 2026 revenue about NT$156.51 hundred million; gross margin 42.2%

quarterly_data.signal: Management (Q&A answers, speakers unlabeled): October shipments are about the same as September and November should start to decline; the customer cut its forecast in September, which management reads as the new phone series not selling well, and customers give no long forecast. Green power is a structural cost because customer contracts require Largan to buy it in proportion to that customer's share; next year's prices are already negotiated, so it can be reflected in prices only the year after. Yield on the new variable-aperture lens now looks OK, and utilization should be full in Q4.

Management (Q&A answers, speakers unlabeled): Largan's fiber array (FA) certification with its customer 'should count as passed', with one customer for volume production; the customer now wants complete FAUs, so Largan will make the FA, buy in PMLA and other parts and couple them into FAUs, and seeks to mount the FAU on the carrier too, acting for this generation like a contractor. The FA pilot line is ready and the customer has visited many times; a newly completed plant will be used entirely for FAU, with lines built by mid next year, and management confirmed ('should be right') that FAU volume production can start in the second half of 2027, the product looking like 'FAU plus carrier' with the carrier board and balls bought in. Multi-row FA is at the sampling stage, for 2028 projects at the earliest and not visible next year, with direct end-customer contact so far only on that next generation; grating-coupling products go to volume production next year while edge coupling is in co-work. FA and FAU are the scarcest CPO parts now; for FAUs, NPO versus CPO makes little difference.

Management (Q&A answers, speakers unlabeled): FA and FAU are the CPO parts in shortest supply, and customers want Largan to build as much capacity as it can; replicating the lines may require outsourcing some capacity because Largan's own may not be enough, while its FA / FAU alignment equipment is built in-house. All the land recently bought has a clear use, for cleanroom production lines, existing buildings will be demolished and rebuilt, and lines started next year will be completed in 2030, all planned for FAU rather than smartphone lenses.

Management (Q&A answers, speakers unlabeled): the next periscope-lens upgrade is likely in 2028, not 2027, and is already in trial production; the main camera has a component upgrade in 2027 that is sampling. The customer's next launch begins pulling around October but cannot make up for the September cut, and Largan cannot see next year's demand.
